{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I almost didn't go to that party—I was tired and it was raining. I made myself go because I'd promised. Met my wife that night. That one reluctant decision to keep a small promise gave me my three children and the life I have now.

CANDIDATE A:
I was excited about that party—I'd been looking forward to it all week. The weather was perfect and I felt energetic. I went eagerly because I'd heard great people would be there. Met my wife that night. But I would have met someone eventually anyway through my active social life. The party was one of many opportunities I pursued deliberately.

CANDIDATE B:
I nearly skipped the open house for an apartment I couldn't afford. Went anyway, just to see the neighborhood. The seller mentioned she needed someone to watch her cat while she traveled. That conversation led to a friendship, then a business partnership, then the company that made me financially independent.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:18"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both involve an initial reluctance to attend an event, followed by an unexpected opportunity that significantly changes the person's life."}
